current.title: Half Of Americans Now Own A Passport -- Up From Just 5% In 1990
current.hook: New Jersey alone is already at 68%.
current.closing: Half the country's ready to leave. The other half isn't.
current.question: Do you actually have a valid passport right now? Tell me below.

segments.say: In 1990, just 5% of Americans owned a passport. Today it's 48% -- almost half the country has one.

segments.topic: how many Americans get a passport now
segments.say: The government can barely keep up -- it issued 24 million passports in 2023, then broke that record with 27.3 million in 2025.
It's not even across the map, though. New Jersey alone sits at 68% -- 20 points above the national average.

judge.one_line: This is a stack of generic machines and charts with a mascot perched on them, and the numbers contradict each other: the hook says 48% while the VO says New Jersey, and the scale says 22.1M while the VO says 27.3M.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3 to seg0:end): the header shows '2023 48%' while the VO and caption say 'New Jersey ... 68%'. The picture and the words disagree from frame 1, and a slow empty block stack is not a reason to stay.
seg2:start: the scale shows 22.1M FY2025 vs 19.5M FY2023, but the VO says 24M and 27.3M. It then hard-cuts to a bar chart with the correct numbers, so the video shows two conflicting sets of values.
seg3: '68.1%' is dark text on a light-blue circle with a doubled or smeared glyph edge, and it is unreadable on a phone.
The mascot only perches on top of marks (block stack, bars, bubble, scale pan) with his arms up. He never does a bit tied to a stat.
seg4 re-shows the NJ vs national comparison from seg3 on a stock seesaw. That is redundant, and the closing line 'half ready to leave' has no visual payoff.
Source lines on seg1:mid and seg3 are too small to read.
fixes: Make the hook show the NJ 68% claim the VO is making, and give it immediate motion: for example, passports flooding a state outline to 68%.
Make the seg2 scale use the narrated values (24M → 27.3M), or drop it in favour of one machine. Show passports being printed or stamped, so the record-breaking volume is physical.
Render the seg3 value in high-contrast ink with a single draw. Replace the circles with a 100-person grid or a stack of passports for NJ vs US.
Give Data a setup → action → payoff bit in each beat: stamping passports, carrying a stack to the top, getting left behind with the 'other half'.
Cut seg4's duplicate comparison, or make it land the closing line visually: a crowd split in half, one side walking to a plane.
Enlarge source text to a legible minimum.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.
